questions.prompt: Having encouraged the soldiers, the general led them into battle.
questions.answer: Adhortātus mīlitēs, dux eōs in proelium dūxit.

questions.prompt: Having feared the storm, the fishermen remained on the shore.
questions.answer: Veritī tempestātem, piscātōrēs in lītore mānsērunt.

questions.prompt: Having set out at dawn, the monk reached the city by night.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce profectus, monachus ad urbem nocte pervēnit.

questions.prompt: Having ravaged the fields of the enemy, Caesar led back his army.
questions.answer: Hostium agrīs vāstātīs, Caesar exercitum redūxit.

questions.prompt: Once camp had been pitched, the soldiers prepared dinner.
questions.answer: Castrīs positīs, mīlitēs cēnam parāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Having plucked the ripe apples, the boy filled his basket.
questions.answer: Mātūrīs pōmīs dēcerptīs, puer corbem implēvit.

questions.prompt: Once the signal had been heard, the horsemen made a charge.
questions.answer: Signō audītō, equitēs impetum fēcērunt.

questions.prompt: When he had arrived there, he pitched a camp.
questions.answer: Eō cum advēnisset, castra posuit.

questions.prompt: The enemy, who had burst into the city, set fire to the temples.
questions.answer: Hostēs, quī in urbem irrūperant, templa incendērunt.

questions.prompt: When the general had encouraged his men, they fought bravely.
questions.answer: Cum dux suōs adhortātus esset, mīlitēs fortiter pugnāvērunt.

questions.prompt: When the storm had ceased, the merchants set out again.
questions.answer: Cum tempestās cessāvisset, mercātōrēs iterum profectī sunt.

questions.prompt: The fugitive was pursued through the whole forest.
questions.answer: Fugitīvus per tōtam silvam agitābātur.

questions.prompt: The camp was being attacked at night by the barbarians.
questions.answer: Castra nocte ā barbarīs temptābantur.

questions.prompt: The name of the traitor was being overwhelmed by oblivion.
questions.answer: Nōmen prōditōris oblīviōne obruēbātur.

questions.prompt: The brave leader is admired, but the coward is hated.
questions.answer: Dux fortis admīrātiōnī est, ignāvus autem in odiō.

questions.prompt: One cannot know everything.
questions.answer: Omnia scīre nōn possīs.

questions.prompt: If one seeks virtue, one will find true happiness.
questions.answer: Sī virtūtem quaerās, vēram fēlīcitātem inveniās.

questions.prompt: You would think that the whole city was on fire.
questions.answer: Putēs tōtam urbem ārdēre.

questions.prompt: By working hard, one wins lasting glory.
questions.answer: Ācriter labōrandō perpetuam glōriam adipīscāris.

questions.prompt: Having feared the wrath of the gods, the priest fled from the temple.
questions.answer: Deōrum īram veritus, sacerdōs ē templō fūgit.

questions.prompt: Having set out at first light, the messenger reached the city before night.
questions.answer: Prīmā lūce profectus, nūntius ante noctem ad urbem pervēnit.

questions.prompt: When you are fortunate, you are envied by many.
questions.answer: Cum fēlīx sīs, multīs in invidiā es.

questions.prompt: Having captured the enemy's city, the victorious soldiers burned the temples.
questions.answer: Urbe hostium captā, mīlitēs victōrēs templa incendērunt.

questions.prompt: When he had encouraged his men, the leader gave the signal for battle.
questions.answer: Cum suōs adhortātus esset, dux signum proeliī dedit.

questions.prompt: This poet is admired by all for his singular charm.
questions.answer: Hic poēta ob singulārem lepōrem omnibus admīrātiōnī est.

questions.prompt: The things which you do not understand you should not lightly despise.
questions.answer: Ea quae nōn intellegās nē facile contemnās.
